paragraphs: Edovo provides free rehabilitation, upskilling, and education to incarcerated people in America. The organization describes its status as a nonprofit. Its programming is accessible on every connected device in jails and prisons, at no cost to the incarcerated learner.

Material runs from basic literacy and GED preparation to college courses and high-demand vocational training. The organization operates exclusively in the corrections space. Facility staff get tools to assess learner progress, create assignments, and digitize programs. Time served can turn into high school diplomas, college credits, workforce certifications, and earned-time credits. Other work prepares returning citizens for life outside prison.

One page states that it serves over a thousand correctional facilities and nearly a million incarcerated learners nationwide. Another page puts the count at 1,500+ prisons and jails across America. The site traces the organization to founder Brian Hill and the idea that breaking the cycle of incarceration starts with access to education. Learner testimonials are published with likenesses changed by AI to protect privacy.
